ms.report:
Our envisioned outcomes of this Milestone were as follows:
・Working groups formed for a) Web3 adoption, b) Open governance, and c) Cross-chain interoperability.
・Each working group self-organized, handling their own planning and brainstorming, community engagement, and topics to be researched and discussed.
・Ideation completed to define how generated knowledge will be made available and usable to community members afterwards.
・Reporting and communication of monthly progress.

These are our achievements for the month of April:

Fully setup and active Workgroups
・Working groups are up and running:
・Web3 adoption run by Luuu and Peter
・Open governance run by Viktor and Felix
・Cross-chain interoperability run by Frank and Mark

Finalized plan on Knowledge Management
・Each working group is working autonomously and handles their own note taking and reporting. We are in constant contact over our core team channel on Discord and gather once a month for a knowledge sharing session.
・We have a shared Drive folder where the meeting recordings go. Read.ai software is set up to listen in on the meetings and to generate a summary in the end.
・The knowledge mined from the working groups is consolidated into one report, a living document that we are shaping throughout the project and that, in the end, will work as a blueprint for anyone who wishes to take our learning points in action.

Monthly recorded and published progress report with Team members
・See the recordings from the April knowledge sharing meeting here:
・Adoption working group
・Governance working group
・Interoperability working group

Other emerging outcomes and progress:
・This was not a planned deliverable but we have realized that there needs to be some sort of simple website where we can direct people to learn more.
・Here is the draft website and documentation (work in progress).
・We have also started attracting attention from key players in both ecosystems and some notable individuals are starting to join the buddi

ms.report:
Introduction
It has been unclear to us what is required to pass this M3 milestone review. After consulting with IOG we received this response from Roberta: "The reason there is one no-approval of the PoA is that the evidence is not collected in the latest PoA but you need to jump between the old submission and the new one to see one. What you are asked to do, is that the previous evidence and the one listed in the latest one are all together and then you will need to resubmit the PoA."
Therefore, this final PoA submission for Milestone 3 includes first all of the required clarifications and then the original PoA report.
The three questions were:
・What are the recent efforts? Monthly recorded and published progress report with Team members only includes content from May... Where are the ones for June and July, and also August.
・Can you also summarize 'Clear plans and use cases for effective collaborations' --- there are far too many documents to peruse and identify.
・"Clear plans and use cases for effective collaborations" can you point to the page in the report?

Our answers:
・ We finished the work we had committed to by the end of July and wrote the final report in August. Once this M3 is approved, we can proceed to close out the project. To alleviate the milestone reviewer’s doubts regarding content creation evidence, the section below from the final report includes the recordings of the uniFires public calls and meetings.
・We realized that three autonomous working groups' reports are difficult to follow and, therefore, we captured everything in the same shared final report. It includes a lot of the pain points (challenges) and solutions (recommendations). These are outlined, chapter by chapter.
・We acknowledge the fact that this part of the milestone is poorly formulated. We apologize for the confusion it has created. Please refer to the final report for all the details about our key takeaways and recommendations, specifically in the Conclusion chapter at the end
